Amid progress on vaccinations and strong policy support, indicators of economic activity and employment have strengthened. Relative to standard policy benchmarks (e.g., Clarida, Galí, and Gertler-style reaction functions and Taylor-rule guidance), the FOMC’s commitment to average inflation targeting (Powell, Jackson Hole 2020) and explicit forward guidance at the zero lower bound, together with ongoing QE ($80B Treasuries, $40B MBS), is distinctly dovish. Such makeup strategies and asset purchases are designed to keep real rates low and compress term premia, supporting credit and risk-taking, which is typically associated with positive market sentiment. At the same time, the statement’s emphasis on “transitory” inflation and persistent virus-related risks aligns with the literature on elevated policy uncertainty during COVID-19, tempering excessive optimism. Net effect: moderately positive, growth-supportive tone with risk-aware caveats.
